dashboard.title: Science, Technology and Innovation Strategy for Africa
dashboard.intro: Continental monitoring of the STISA 2034 results framework. Member States set their own baselines and targets, and only returns the African Union Commission has published appear here. Data completeness measures how much of each return arrived. Target progress measures how the values that arrived stand against those self-set targets. The two percentages use different denominators, and each figure states which one it used.

schedule.title: STISA 2034 reporting schedule
schedule.description: Member States report in four official reporting years across two implementation phases. Data entry is only possible while a cycle is open.
schedule.footnote: Phase 1 covers implementation 2025–2029 and reports in 2026 and 2028. Phase 2 covers 2030–2034 and reports in 2030 and 2033.

regional.title: Regional comparison
regional.description: For each African Union region, data completeness is the share of required indicator values reported by Member States that sent at least one value. States that published nothing are counted in the label under the region name, not inside the percentage, so a high bar does not mean the whole region reported. Target progress is the unweighted average of the scores that could be calculated. Each Member State counts equally.

sectors.title: Sector and priority performance
sectors.description: The 16 categories in scope, grouped into three result levels: outcomes, sectorial priorities, and strategic priorities. The five Impact-level rows in the MEAL Plan are not collected. For each category, data completeness is how full the published returns are, and target progress is the average score of values that could be compared with a target. A complete return can still be far from its targets, and a missing value is not treated as zero progress.

heatmap.title: Reporting coverage by Member State and sector
heatmap.description: Each cell is the share of that category’s required indicators the Member State reported. It is coverage, not progress toward targets. An empty cell means nothing was reported for that category. It is not a score of zero.
heatmap.columnNote: Each column is one of the 16 categories in scope. The Impact level is not included.

trend.title: Historical reporting trend
trend.description: One point per reporting year that has published data: 2026, 2028, 2030 and 2033. Completeness in a year is measured among Member States that reported at least one value, so a year with few reporting states can still show high completeness. Target progress is the unweighted average of scores that could be calculated. Years with no published return are omitted rather than drawn as zero.
trend.empty: Historical comparison becomes available once a second reporting cycle has been published.

leaderboard.title: Member State reporting
leaderboard.description: For each Member State, data completeness is how many of its required indicators were reported. sectors.title: STISA 2034 results framework
sectors.description: This platform collects 16 categories across three result levels — outcomes, sectorial priorities, and strategic priorities — transcribed from Annexure 1 of the Implementation Plan. The Impact level is outside the scope of this platform and is not collected. Open a category to see each indicator, how completely it was reported, and how the reported values score against the targets Member States set for themselves.

sectors.clarificationBody: The STISA 2034 MEAL Plan states these indicators in a form that a single reported value cannot fully capture — for example a cell containing two distinct measurements, a row repeated verbatim elsewhere, or a required breakdown that is never defined. They are stored exactly as printed and flagged rather than reinterpreted.

explainer.title: How these two percentages were calculated
explainer.intro: Data completeness and target progress answer different questions and use different denominators. Completeness asks how much of the expected return arrived. Target progress asks how the values that arrived stand against the targets their Member States set.
explainer.completenessWhat: Share of required indicator values that were actually reported.
explainer.completenessBody: The denominator is every required indicator in this {scope}, multiplied by the Member States that reported at least one value here. A Member State that published nothing for this {scope} is omitted from this percentage. The count of reporting states is shown separately. Values left blank or marked not applicable stay in the denominator, which is why completeness falls. They are not filled in as zero.
explainer.progressWhat: Unweighted average of the scores that could be calculated.
explainer.progressBody: Each reported value is scored with that indicator’s own formula. A count closes the gap from its baseline to its target. A change measure is compared with the target change. A milestone is 100% if achieved and 0% if reported as not achieved. An indicator with no methodology in the MEAL Plan is not scored. Each scored value counts equally, whether the Member State is large or small. 100% means the target was met. A score above 100% means it was exceeded and is not cut back to 100%. A result that moved away from the target is shown as 0%.
explainer.statesReported: Member States that reported at least one value here
explainer.valuesReceived: values reported with a usable figure
explainer.couldNotScore: reported, but no score could be calculated
explainer.missingNote: The {missing} blank or not-applicable answers stay inside the completeness denominator, which is why completeness can be below 100%. They are not inserted as zero into the target-progress average.
explainer.unscoredNote: {count} reported values are published but left out of the target-progress average, because a score would require a methodology, a target, or a current value the return does not provide. Leaving them out is not the same as scoring them at zero.
explainer.allScoredNote: Every one of the {count} reported values produced a score, so the target-progress average uses the same count as the values received. Completeness can still be lower, because blank and not-applicable answers remain in its denominator.

methodology.title: Methodology
methodology.intro: How indicator definitions, reported values and continental aggregates on this platform are produced, and the limits of what they can support.
methodology.sourcesDescription: Implementation Plan STISA 2034 — Annexure 1: MEAL Plan, printed pages 37–40.
methodology.sourcesBody: Every indicator on this platform is a verbatim transcription of one row of the MEAL Plan results table. Indicator text has not been renamed, merged, split, de-duplicated or reinterpreted, and the source document's own punctuation, capitalisation and spelling inconsistencies are preserved.
methodology.countBodyAfter: Separately, the STISA 2034 programme documentation refers to {stated}. The candidate rows are {candidates}.
methodology.notSuppliedTitle: What the source document does not supply
methodology.notSuppliedDescription: The MEAL Plan table has three columns: Indicator, Baseline Data (2024) and Target Value. The latter two are blank for every row.
methodology.notSuppliedBody: The document therefore supplies no indicator codes, no definitions, no units, no data types, no calculation methodologies, no baselines, no targets and no data sources. This platform handles that as follows:
methodology.codesBody: are assigned by this platform in printed row order and are labelled as such. They are not official AU codes.
methodology.unitsBody: are inferred from each indicator’s own wording (“Number of…” → count, “Percentage change in…” → percentage) and every inference is recorded against the indicator.
methodology.baselinesBody: are supplied by the reporting Member State, not by the strategy document. Cross-country comparison of target progress is therefore comparison against self-set targets.
methodology.definitionsBody: remain empty until the African Union issues them.
methodology.missingDescription: Missing values are never counted as zero.
methodology.missingBody: Each indicator response carries an explicit state:
methodology.stateNotReported: the Member State could not supply the figure.
methodology.stateNotApplicable: the indicator does not apply, with a stated reason.
methodology.stateInvalid: a value was supplied but failed validation.
methodology.formula:
Average = Sum of valid reported values
          ÷ Number of valid reported values
methodology.exclusionBefore: Values that are missing, null, not reported or not applicable are excluded from both the numerator and the denominator. Every figure on this platform is displayed with the denominator it was computed over — for example
methodology.exclusionExample: “Regional progress: 68% — based on 8 of 10 countries reporting”
methodology.exclusionAfter: — so an incomplete dataset can never present itself as a complete one.
methodology.completenessException: That exclusion applies to averages, including target progress. Data completeness is the exception: blank and not-applicable answers stay in its denominator, because completeness is the share of required values that arrived. Removing them from the denominator would make every partial return look complete.
methodology.progressDescription: Each indicator is scored with its own formula. The headline “target progress” is then the unweighted average of those scores.
methodology.progressBody: The results framework mixes counts, composite index scores, shares, percentage changes, ratios and yes-or-no milestones. One formula applied to all of them would produce meaningless numbers, so the engine dispatches on the indicator’s own method and direction. 100% means that indicator’s target was met. The average does not weight Member States by population, and it does not mix in values that could not be scored.
methodology.progressFloor: Progress is floored at 0% — a regression reads as no progress toward the target rather than as a negative figure — but is deliberately not capped at 100%, so over-achievement stays visible.
methodology.progressCalloutBefore: Where the source document defines no methodology for an indicator, the platform returns
methodology.progressCalloutAfter: and states why, rather than applying a default formula. Those indicators are still displayed and their reported values are still published — they are simply excluded from progress averages.
methodology.ambiguitiesTitle: Known ambiguities in the source framework
methodology.ambiguitiesDescription: Recorded against each indicator and surfaced in the sector pages.
methodology.ambOverlaps: Rows measuring substantially the same construct
methodology.ambContinental: Rows worded continentally but reported nationally
methodology.ambBasis: Rows whose measurement basis is unclear
methodology.ambUnit: Rows whose unit is never specified
methodology.ambiguitiesNote: These are preserved rather than resolved. Resolving them requires official guidance from the African Union Commission; inventing an interpretation would silently change what Member States are being asked to measure.
methodology.publicBodyBefore: A Member State return passes through draft, submitted, under review, approved and published.
methodology.publicBodyStrong: Only published returns enter public analytics.
methodology.publicBodyAfter: Drafts, submitted-but-unreviewed and approved-but-unpublished returns are never visible on these pages, and are never included in continental, regional or sector figures.
methodology.publicHistory: Each reporting cycle is stored separately, so a Member State's 2026 return is never overwritten by its 2028 return and historical comparison across 2026, 2028, 2030 and 2033 remains possible.
methodology.countBodyScope: , of which this platform collects {inScope}. The five Impact-level rows are outside the scope of this platform and are not collected from Member States.
methodology.compoundNote: Splitting any one compound cell into its two constituent statements yields 81. The source document provides no numbering, so the split cannot be made without official guidance.

progressNote.NO_METHODOLOGY: The STISA 2034 MEAL Plan defines no calculation methodology for this indicator, so the reported number is published and left unscored. It is left out of every target-progress average rather than given a guessed percentage.
progressNote.NO_ACTUAL: No current value was reported for this indicator, so there is nothing to compare with the target. The gap is left blank. It is not treated as zero progress.
progressNote.NO_TARGET: A current value was reported, but no target was set, so there is no endpoint to measure against. The value is published and left out of the target-progress average.
progressNote.NON_NUMERIC: This indicator is text, a web address, or a category. It has no numeric distance to a target, so it is published as reported and left out of target-progress averages.
progressNote.DEGENERATE_TARGET_ZERO: The target is zero, so progress cannot be expressed as a percentage of that target. The reported value is kept and the indicator is left unscored.
progressNote.DEGENERATE_EQUAL_ENDS: The baseline and the target are the same number, so there is no gap to close and progress cannot be expressed as a percentage of that gap. The reported value is kept and the indicator is left unscored.
progressNote.DEGENERATE_ACTUAL_ZERO: A lower result is better and the reported value is zero. Dividing the target by zero is undefined, so the indicator is left unscored instead of being shown as infinite progress.
progressNote.DEGENERATE_NON_FINITE: The baseline, target, and reported value do not produce a finite percentage. The reported value is kept and the indicator is left unscored.
progressNote.BINARY_YES: This is a yes-or-no milestone. It was reported as achieved, which scores 100%. An unanswered milestone is left blank; a reported “no” scores 0% because that is a real answer, not missing data.
progressNote.BINARY_NO: This is a yes-or-no milestone. It was reported as not yet achieved, which scores 0%. That zero is a real result. An unanswered milestone is left blank instead of being scored.
progressNote.CHANGE: The reported number is already a change, and the target is the change the Member State aimed for. Progress is the reported change divided by the target change. Record a reduction as a negative number. A baseline is not applied again, because that would count the change twice. 100% means the targeted change was reached. Above 100% means it was exceeded. Movement in the opposite direction scores 0%.
progressNote.CLOSENESS: Progress measures closeness to the target from either side. Exactly on target is 100%. A result 20% of the target away, whether above or below, scores 80%. The baseline is not used. Once the distance reaches the size of the target, the score is shown as 0%.
progressNote.LEVEL_NO_BASELINE_HIGHER: No baseline was recorded, so this is the reported value as a share of the target, not the share of a baseline-to-target gap that has been closed. 100% means the target level was reached. Above 100% means it was exceeded.
progressNote.LEVEL_NO_BASELINE_LOWER: No baseline was recorded, and a lower number is an improvement. The score is the target divided by the reported value. Reaching the target is 100%. A value below the target scores above 100%.
progressNote.LEVEL_GAP_HIGHER: A higher number is an improvement. Progress is the share of the gap from the baseline to the target that has been closed: (reported value − baseline) ÷ (target − baseline). 100% means the target was reached. Above 100% means it was passed. A value at or below the baseline scores 0%, so a worsening is not shown as a negative percentage.
progressNote.LEVEL_GAP_LOWER: A lower number is an improvement. Progress is the share of the intended reduction that has been achieved: (baseline − reported value) ÷ (baseline − target). 100% means the target was reached. A value that moved upward instead scores 0%.
progressNote.LEVEL_NO_BASELINE_ASSUMED: No baseline was recorded, and the source does not say whether a higher or lower result is better. The score therefore treats a higher result as better and is the reported value as a share of the target. 100% means the target level was reached.
progressNote.LEVEL_GAP_ASSUMED: The source does not say whether a higher or lower result is better, so the score assumes a higher result is an improvement. It is the share of the gap from the baseline to the target that has been closed. 100% means the target was reached. A value at or below the baseline scores 0%.

methodHelp.PERCENTAGE_CHANGE: The number reported is already a percentage change. Progress compares that change with the target change, and does not apply a baseline a second time.
methodHelp.PERCENTAGE_POINT_CHANGE: The number reported is already a change in percentage points. Progress compares that change with the target change in points.
methodHelp.ABSOLUTE_COUNT: Progress is how much of the gap from the baseline count to the target count has been closed. If no baseline was set, the score is the reported count as a share of the target count.
methodHelp.ABSOLUTE_VALUE: Progress is how much of the gap from the baseline value to the target value has been closed. If no baseline was set, the score is the reported value as a share of the target.
methodHelp.SHARE_OF_TOTAL: The reported number is a share of some total, such as a percentage of the population. Progress treats that share as a level: it closes the gap from the baseline share to the target share when a baseline exists.
methodHelp.INDEX_SCORE: The reported number is a composite index. Progress is how much of the gap from the baseline score to the target score has been closed.
methodHelp.RATIO: The reported number is a ratio. Progress is how much of the gap from the baseline ratio to the target ratio has been closed, unless the indicator is defined as closer-to-target.
methodHelp.BINARY_ACHIEVEMENT: This is a milestone. Achieved scores 100%. Reported as not achieved scores 0%. Left unanswered is not a score.
methodHelp.CUSTOM: A custom formula has been flagged but not defined, so this indicator is published and left unscored.
methodHelp.UNDEFINED: The MEAL Plan does not say how to turn this indicator into a percentage of its target, so it is published and left unscored.

directionHelp.HIGHER_IS_BETTER: A larger reported number is an improvement.
directionHelp.LOWER_IS_BETTER: A smaller reported number is an improvement. When the indicator is itself a change, record a reduction as a negative number.
directionHelp.TARGET_IS_BETTER: The best result is the target itself. Being above it and being below it reduce the score by the same amount.
directionHelp.NOT_APPLICABLE: The source does not say whether a higher or lower result is better. Where a score is still produced, it assumes a higher result is an improvement, and the note under each value says so.

method.UNDEFINED: Not defined in the source document

provenance.NOT_PROVIDED: not provided by the source document
